title: introduce-retry-advice-v2-and-idempotency-ttl-refresh
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Context and motivation: Customer integrations that multiplex streamed tool/function calls observed ambiguous retry guidance and premature idempotency session expiry during long-running client interactions. This led to duplicate tool invocations when clients retried after partial stream failures and to noisy operator alerts when clients refreshed connections frequently. The OpenAI compatibility layer currently surfaces Retry-After and a minimal 429 envelope, but lacks a machine-readable, compact retry-advice payload and a safe mechanism for clients to keep idempotency sessions alive without reusing long-lived secrets.

Summary of changes: This PR introduces a v2 retry advice header/payload and a short-lived idempotency-lease refresh flow in the OpenAI-shim. Key changes: 1) X-Redwood-Retry-Advice: a structured, base64-encoded JSON token (compact envelope) that carries server-side backoff window, preferred backoff algorithm (linear/exponential), and an optional soft-capacity-tag for routing decisions. 2) Idempotency session TTL and refresh endpoint: clients can create session-scoped leases (Idempotency-Session: <opaque-id>) returned with a TTL and a refresh_token; a short HTTPS POST to /v1/compat/idempotency/refresh with the refresh_token extends the lease. 3) Streaming semantics: when a streamed tool call fails mid-frame, the server will emit an immediate retry-advice frame (server-side) in the stream pre-close which includes whether a fresh idempotency lease is required or if the existing lease remains valid. 4) Backwards compatibility: if clients don't understand X-Redwood-Retry-Advice, the shim still returns Retry-After and existing 429 behavior unchanged. 5) Observability: new metrics retry_advice_emitted, idempotency_lease_created, idempotency_lease_refreshed and corresponding dashboard panels.

Files and touchpoints (high-level): 
- services/openai-compat/handlers/retry_advice.go: implements v2 advice token generation and validation. 
- services/openai-compat/handlers/idempotency_session.go: session lifecycle and refresh endpoint. 
- runtime/streaming/stream_router.go: inserts retry-advice frames into stream error paths and annotates stream close reasons. 
- api/swagger/compat.yaml: documents the new refresh endpoint and retry-advice header (kept behind experimental flag). 
- observability/dashboards/retry-advice.json: new dashboards and panels. 

Compatibility and rollout: The new header is behind a feature flag (compat.retry_advice_v2) on the control plane. Default remains v1 Retry-After + existing 429 envelope. Gradual rollout plan: enable for 10% of traffic for 48 hours, evaluate duplicated-invocation metric and client error rates, then ramp to 100% over 7 days if healthy. The refresh endpoint is opt-in and rate-limited per account (configurable by tier).

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover advice token encoding/decoding and TTL enforcement. Integration harness runs simulated intermittent stream failures and verifies: idempotency session stays valid when refresh token used, duplicate tool calls do not occur when lease is refreshed, and non-upgrade clients observe unchanged 429/Retry-After behavior. Load tests executed in benchmark-lab showed <1% p99 latency increase for small token sizes and negligible CPU overhead for advice token issuance at 2000 RPS.

Security and privacy notes: Advice tokens are opaque and HMAC-signed with short expiry to avoid replay; refresh tokens are single-use and rotated on each refresh. Leases are scoped to account+route to avoid cross-tenant reuse. KMS-backed keys are used for signing. Docs and migration notes call out developers should not persist refresh tokens long-term and should treat them as ephemeral credentials.

Rollout checklist: 
- [x] Control plane feature flag gating added
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks and load validation
- [x] Observability panels and alerts
- [x] Docs PR in redwood-docs (linked below)

Related work and references: ENG-1248 (rate guidance consolidation), ENG-1310 (idempotency UX for streamed tools). See also linear note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1248/retry-advice-consolidation and docs PR: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-4823-openai-compat-retry-advice-v2.json

Migration guidance for SDKs: SDKs (python/ts/go) should consume X-Redwood-Retry-Advice when present, prefer the embedded backoff_window field to compute next attempt, and use the refresh endpoint to extend idempotency leases prior to reconnection. Example pseudo-flow included in docs.

Merge notes: Squash-merge chosen to keep history compact; deploy will include a small DB migration to add idempotency_sessions table (backfilled lazily).

reviews: Dmitri Karpov (commented on 2025-01-10): Nice compact token design. Question: why base64 rather than compact JOSE? Response: chosen to keep header size small and avoid parsing chase in edge proxies; token is HMAC-signed and schema versioned.

Leah O'Connor (requested changes on 2025-01-11): Please add rate-limits on the refresh endpoint and a clear error mapping for expired refresh_token. Response: Added rate-limiting and explicit 410 semantics for expired refresh tokens; updated swagger.
Marco Ruiz (approved on 2025-01-12): Verified integration tests and load numbers. Approving for merge.
release_notes: Adds a machine-readable retry advice header (X-Redwood-Retry-Advice v2) and an opt-in idempotency session lease + refresh endpoint to reduce duplicate tool invocations during streamed failures. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind compat.retry_advice_v2.
